subject: Post-call recap: PrismPay discovery — latency & throughput qualification
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Evan Liu <evan@prismpay.com>, Priya Singh <priya@prismpay.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-08-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: PrismPay discovery — latency & throughput qualification

Hi Evan / Priya — thanks again for a focused discussion this morning. Quick recap of the core points I captured and the proposed next steps so we have alignment before the technical deep-dive: 

Summary of pain / goals
- Customer-facing routing & authorization flows require sub-200ms 95th percentile for single-turn intent classification (avg payload ~60 tokens) to avoid UI jank in mobile/web flows.
- Peak patterns: synchronous user traffic with short bursts (2–4s sustained at peak) and daily peak in PST morning; current infra can't keep up at scale.
- Multi-turn session state: prioritizing correctness + KV-cache reuse across 3–10 turns per session.
- Data controls: customer PII must remain in their VPC for some flows; logs/audit access required for specific endpoints.

Redwood’s initial assessment (high level)
- Two viable deployment modes: Dedicated pool (predictable throughput) or Private VPC for strict residency + KMS. Hosted API workable for early POC but will need caching + canary routing for p95 guarantees.
- Model recommendations: start POC on a 13B chat model quantized to 4-bit for latency-sensitive endpoints; evaluate results vs a 70B if quality gaps appear.
- SLO targets we discussed today (confirm): p50 ~ 40ms, p95 <= 150ms for single-turn @ 128 tokens; sustained throughput target 200–350 req/s depending on route.

Immediate asks from Redwood
1) Confirm the two routes you care about: (A) user-facing auth/classification (low latency); (B) async batch scoring (throughput).
2) Provide a sample traffic histogram (RPS over 24h + median/peak concurrency) or a short CSV of request timestamps if available.
3) Confirm whether any flows must remain inside your VPC from day-1 (PII requirement).

Next steps & PoC scope
- Redwood to deliver: 1) PoC runbook + capacity estimate, 2) mutual action plan (timeline + owners), 3) cost ballpark for Dedicated and Private options, 4) proposed model/quantization profile and KV cache strategy.
- Proposed timeline: 4-week POC, week 0 discovery + data ingestion, week 1 baseline perf, week 2 optimizations (batching/caching/quantization), week 3 validation + handoff.

Attachments: prismpay_poc_sla_matrix.xlsx (empty template attached)

Please confirm the SLO numbers above and supply the traffic sample when convenient. I’ll coordinate a 60–90 minute technical deep-dive with our infra & runtime leads once we have your traffic profile.

Thanks — looking forward to moving quickly on this.

Best,
Sean Gallagher

Thanks Sean — echoing the recap and adding technical detail so the PoC can be scoped accurately. I pulled some quick estimates below; these are first-pass and will be finalized after we see your traffic sample.

Key technical constraints to confirm
- Typical prompt lengths and completion lengths per route (we assumed 60 tokens request, 64 tokens response for low-latency route).
- Acceptable batching window: adding 10–25ms of latency for batching may be ok for some routes but not for auth flows.

Preliminary topology options
1) Hosted + Edge routing (fastest time-to-value)
   - Prefix/KV caching enabled for multi-turn sessions to reduce model calls by ~40–70% depending on repeat prompts.
   - Auto-burst to Dedicated capacity under sustained peak; fallback to smaller model when Dedicated saturated.
2) Dedicated GPU pool (recommended for steady-state predictable latency)
   - Config: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (multi-instance serving) for 300 req/s @ p95 <= 150ms with 13B 4-bit quantized model (est).
   - Continuous batching with route-level latency SLOs; warm pool maintained for cold-starts <200ms.
3) Private VPC (strict data residency; recommended if you need KMS + audit logs inside your network)
   - Same runtime but customer-controlled networking and HSM integration; adds ~5–15ms network overhead depending on cloud region.

Caching & KV recommendations
- Use Redis-backed prefix cache for session tokens + on-host KV cache for per-GPU fast hits. We’ve attached an example KV hit-rate profile from a similar POC (kv_cache_profile.png).
- Expect effective reduction in model calls of 30–55% for conversational e-commerce traffic.

Model strategy & quality ramp
- Start POC on 13B chat model quantized to int4 (4-bit) to validate latency goals. If quality issues surface on named-entity extraction and paraphrase resolution, iterate to 70B or apply targeted rerank/ensembling for the small percentage of high-risk flows.

Operational constraints
- Observability: token-level tracing + per-route latency breakdown will be enabled for the PoC; need list of routes you want instrumented.
- Rollouts: we recommend canary (5%→25%→100%) with automatic rollback on regression.

Action items (Irene)
- I’ll prepare a capacity/cost estimate by EOD Friday once we get the 24h traffic sample.
- I’ll also include a PoC runbook with exact infra sizes and the expected warm-up script to minimize cold-start variance.

--
Irene Choi
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com

Thanks Sean and Irene — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side before the PoC runbook: 

Traffic & concurrency
- We’ll extract a 72h sample and send it by EOD today. For clarity: normal day RPS is ~40–60; peak bursts historically hit 280–320 RPS for ~10–60 seconds during promotional pushes.
- Concurrency per user session is low (1–5), but the number of parallel sessions can spike quickly during peaks.

Data residency
- For routing/auth flows (route A) we need full residency in our VPC due to regional PII controls. Other routes (batch scoring) can be in Hosted.

Operational questions
- Cold start: what warm pool sizes do you recommend to keep cold-starts under 200ms for the low-latency route?
- Cache persistence: can we persist KV cache to local SSD to survive pod restarts and keep hit rates high?

PoC ask
- We agree to the 4-week PoC. Can you produce the mutual action plan and a cost delta between Dedicated vs Private for the baseline config? Also confirm whether you can include a brief (30–45m) session on in-PoC observability (how to interpret token-level traces).

Thanks — Evan
